ledger.what: remove cookie/consent chrome (OneTrust, Cookiebot, Usercentrics, generic cookie-banner ids/classes, any cookie/consent/gdpr-named element inside a fixed/sticky/high-z overlay)
ledger.why: overlay chrome injected by a CMP, not page content; re-added at deploy time

ledger.what: de-carousel slick/swiper/splide/glide: remove clone slides, force real slides visible+static, drop dots/arrows
ledger.why: hidden slides are absent from innerText and clones duplicate it — rotating carousels break byte determinism; the reskin renders all slides statically in DOM order

ledger.what: open every .nsw-accordion panel (unhide its content region, aria-expanded=true)
ledger.why: closed panel text is content; capture-only — the rendered accordion keeps the closed rest state

visibleTextNormalized: HomeSchool lifeStudent opportunities and activities Student opportunities and activities At Fort Street High School, we offer a variety of programs in the classroom and across the school to help students build new skills, make friends and explore new interests. Our programs include: Interest-based Clubs and Committees Academic Competitions Creative and Performing Arts Groups Instrumental Music Programme Duke of Edinburgh Award School sport, athletics and inter-school competitions Debating and Public Speaking Robotics and Maker Society Student leadership opportunities including Student Representative Council At the start of each year there will be a Clubs and Committess Day at lunch time where students can visit the groups in the hall. Students can find out about each club and what they do and sign up to any that they may be interested in. The school encourages all students to participate in two (or more) co-curricular activities, in order to make friendships, develop skills and build confidence and resilience. Schedule of Weekly activities 2026 Monday Tuesday Wednesday Thursday Friday Before School Running Club Wind Orchestra Girls Volleyball training Ultimate Frisbee Netball Club Morning Meditation Symphony Orchestra Drama Club Philosophy Wind Ensemble Breakfast Club Vocal Ensemble Jazz Ensemble Senior Boys Volleyball School Musical Band Running Club Philharmonic Orchestra Lunch SRC Training Band Junior Percussion - Senior Percussion Astronomy Club Environment Committee Girl UP Female Leadership Book Club (once a month) Recorder Ensemble Amnesty/Social Justice Sending Sunshine Club (week B) Stive Diversity Committee After School Debating & Public Speaking Blender Club (3D Modelling) Theatresports Chamber Choir Big Band Jazz Orchestra Year 9/10 English Enrichment Art Studio Concert Band Fitness Club Maker Society (Robotics) Chess Club Overseas Tours keyboard_arrow_down The school has a long history of sister school exchanges with Fortians having the opportunity to host students from Japan, France and Germany, as well as the opportunity to visit these countries on exchange. The Instrumental Music Program also offers students the opportunity to travel and perform across a number of European countries. Language Cultural Tours Students from Years 10 and 11 German and Japanese classes travelled to their fellow sister schools in Berlin and Tokyo during the 2025 September/October holiday period to participate in lessons, cultural activities as well as touring other culturally significant sites. All students were able to use their language skills to enhance understanding of their newfound worlds. Sister-school relationships began with the Georg Büchner Gymnasium (Berlin) in 1999 and Suginami-Sogo High School (Tokyo) from the mid 1980s. Students from these schools will also visit Fort Street High School and the school may request families to billet them while they are here. Billeting is a great way for Fortians to establish friendships with students their own ages and perhaps visit them in their home country at another time. Contact: Ms Lindy Wark Head Teacher - History/Languages Cohen Staffroom IMP European Tour The Instrumental Music Program aims to tour overseas every 3 years, and is generally open to more senior IMP students. Previous tours have seen groups of approximately 100 students performing in Italy, Austria, Croatia, Hungary, The Czech Republic, Slovakia and Slovenia. We performed in some of the most iconic venues in Europe, including singing mass at St Peter’s Basilica in Rome, and a recital in St Mark’s Venice. As well as numerous informal recitals in venues ranging from caves to the Pantheon, we played to packed houses in public concerts in Vienna, Rome, Florence and Venice. "The breadth of opportunities available runs from diverse academic subjects to high-quality extracurricular programs. My children have been able to explore their interests and develop into well-rounded individuals amongst like-minded peers." Elizabeth— a parent of Fort Street High School Need to make a payment? lines: We recognise the Ongoing Custodians of the lands and waterways where we work and live. We pay respect to Elders past and present as ongoing teachers of knowledge, songlines and stories. We strive to ensure every Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander learner in NSW achieves their potential through education.
